drive.cap_rule: every rate is capped at 1000 / sim.Params.t_ref Hz, and kicks pass a dead time of one refractory period (song.dead_time), since stimulated neurons are never refractory in the kernel: the delivered rate is at most lambda / (1 + lambda * t_ref)
drive.forms_why: Ache et al. 2019 (abstract): the giant fiber follows 'a linear function of angular velocity (provided by LC4) and a Gaussian function of angular size (provided by LPLC2)'; the Gaussian's parameters were not read from the paper, so size enters linearly; neither is a measured LC4 or LPLC2 spike rate
drive.grid_why: engineered envelope: LC4 and LPLC2 spike rates to looming are not measured (docs/leads.md, G3). At r/v 10 ms dtheta/dt reaches about 55 rad/s at 63 degrees, so g4 spans no input to the cap; theta reaches 1.1 rad, so g2 spans no input to about 220 Hz. The cell with both gains 0 has no input and is left out: 15 cells.
drive.kicks: per neuron and neural step, Poisson counts at the rate of that step, then the dead time; one kick is about 48 mV. LPLC2's drive steps from 0 to g2 * 0.17 rad at onset, as the disc appears at 10 degrees
drive.sides_why: the recorded side and the disc's azimuth in the 2025 runs are not stated

model.fit: per cell, y = collision time - peak time per seed and r/v; the median over seeds per r/v; ordinary least squares y = alpha * rv - delta over the four r/v
model.graded: a cell stays graded when neither giant fiber fires in the window in any seed and r/v; the recordings are subthreshold, so only responding and graded cells are scored, and the others are reported
model.near_end_why: a peak within 20 ms after the expansion stops follows the stimulus; the share of such peaks is reported per cell and per fly
model.post_why: the window ends 150 ms after the expansion stops (Dombrovski et al. 2025 score 150 ms after onset in their Fig. 1); a later peak is no longer driven by expansion
model.reach_why: a noisy plateau makes the time of the maximum itself arbitrary; the first time at 95% of it is defined the same way in model and data
model.readout: the membrane potential of DNp01(GF)_R and DNp01(GF)_L at every neural step (CpuRuntime.read), a sample standing at the end of its step, filtered as the data (data_rule.filter, the same frame in ms, since the distortion it gives an asymmetric peak grows with r/v and would otherwise bias alpha; the run lasts one frame past the window so the filter's edge stays outside it); per giant fiber the baseline is the mean over pre_ms and the peak time the first sample in the window (after onset to the end of the expansion plus post_ms) at reach of its window maximum above baseline; the run's peak time is the mean of the two
model.responding: a cell responds when, in every seed and r/v, both giant fibers rise by at least sim.Params.w_syn (one synapse's jump at rest): a bar for a defined peak, not for strength
model.timing: a kick at a step reaches the potential at the next; with the sample at the end of its step this is a constant 0.1 to 0.2 ms, which enters delta only
